_comment: Allowlist for check-global-state.py. Each `entries` item documents a thread-local declaration in the plugin/dyncode/linker trees that is NOT plugin-related process-global mutable *compilation* state. The source scan is the only layer that judges thread-local storage, so every thread_local belongs here and never in `binary_symbols`; the gate is run with --strict, which makes an undocumented one a hard failure. Only stack-scoped RAII facades and option-lease owner/depth/digest TLS (no option values) are eligible. A const interface or lookup table is never eligible anywhere in this file: make it `constexpr` so it is constant-initialized into read-only storage. Writable process-storage symbols in the linked compiler are a separate list; see `_binary_symbols_comment`. Session/Task/options/graph/symbol/output/cache-journal payloads must NEVER be allowlisted.

entries.justification: Callback ancestry / re-entrancy depth stack held by a trivially destructible thread-local wrapper. Existing invocation-scope RAII explicitly releases stored elements as it unwinds through the outermost pop; empty between invocations. Carries no Session/Task/artifact payload.

Callback scope stack used only to detect nested callback ancestry and held by a trivially destructible thread-local wrapper. Existing callback-scope RAII explicitly releases stored elements as it unwinds through the outermost pop; empty at rest.

Active-plugin re-entrancy stack held by a trivially destructible thread-local wrapper. Existing callback-scope RAII explicitly releases stored elements as it unwinds through the outermost pop; empty at rest and carries no compilation payload.

entries.lifetime: stack-scoped per VFS query dynamic extent
entries.justification: VFS route/recursion-budget stack held by a trivially destructible thread-local wrapper. Existing query-scope RAII explicitly releases stored elements as it unwinds through the outermost pop; empty at rest and prevents infinite provider recursion. No cached FS state.

entries.lifetime: stack-scoped RAII guard per LinkTask/worker scope
entries.justification: Legacy allocator/diagnostic facade guard. Installed/restored by nestable RAII; cleared on worker join and thread-pool reuse. Never queried by plugin callbacks (they receive explicit task/context handles).
Worker-slot index for context-owned allocator shard selection; set/reset by worker wrapper, zero at rest. No link state.

entries.lifetime: stack-scoped per test link invocation on the calling thread
entries.justification: Test-only callback and opaque context pointer installed immediately before a synchronous Mach-O link and cleared by make_scope_exit on every normal or early return. TLS prevents concurrent test threads from sharing the observation. The hook is not forwarded to linker workers and carries no Session/Task/options/graph/symbol/output/cache-journal payload.
LLVMOptionLease owner/depth/digest bookkeeping only. Holds no actual cl::opt values; used to enforce shared-default / exclusive-nondefault nesting rules.
Per-thread longjmp buffer for merge fatal-error recovery; installed/cleared around each merge, carries no cross-invocation compilation state.

_binary_symbols_comment: Writable *process* data symbols in the shipped `neverc` binary (build-dir/bin/neverc) whose name is under neverc::plugin/neverc::dyncode but which are NOT process-global mutable compilation state. Thread-local symbols never belong here: the binary layer skips them, because ELF names one `.tbss` object where Mach-O emits a `__thread_vars` descriptor plus a `$tlv$init` storage symbol, and judging that here made the gate pass on one host and fail on another for identical sources. Put them in `entries` instead. Eligible categories: (a) address-only LLVM legacy-pass identity tokens (`char Pass::ID`), (b) const objects whose vtable pointer forces a relocation into writable storage, (c) synchronization primitives with no compilation state, and (d) foreign-runtime descriptors that the foreign ABI requires to have static writable lifetime but that contain no NeverC compilation payload. A const interface or lookup table is NOT eligible: make it `constexpr` so it is constant-initialized into read-only storage instead of adding it here. Session/Task/options/graph/symbol/output/cache-journal payloads must NEVER appear here.

binary_symbols.justification: `char DynCodeMIRTransformPass::ID` -- address-only LLVM legacy machine-pass identity for the built-in MIR transform provider; only its address is taken, never its value written.
`char DynCodeMIRVerifierPass::ID` -- address-only LLVM legacy machine-pass identity for the sealed MIR final-verify gate; only its address is taken, never its value written.
`char IRToMIRPipelinePass::ID` -- address-only LLVM legacy pass identity.
`char MIRToMCPipelinePass::ID` -- address-only LLVM legacy pass identity.
`char PluginMachinePass::ID` -- address-only LLVM legacy pass identity.
`char PluginMachineModulePass::ID` -- address-only LLVM legacy pass identity.

`static const BuiltinLinkerScriptProvider Provider` -- a stateless const provider singleton holding no data members. It cannot be made `constexpr`: LinkerScriptProvider has a virtual destructor, so the type is not a literal type, and the vtable pointer needs a relocation regardless. Writable-section placement is the vtable pointer, not compilation state.
`static std::shared_mutex Gate` -- the process-serial gate guarding LLVM cl::opt install/restore. A lock, not compilation state; the spec explicitly permits sync primitives without compilation state.

Monotonic atomic counter used only to observe entry into the option gate's blocking path in concurrency tests. It carries no option, session, task, graph, artifact, or compiler payload and never affects compilation behavior.
`std::once_flag InterpreterOnce` serializes CPython initialization. It stores no session, task, plugin, option, graph, artifact, or compiler payload.

CPython's `PyModuleDef` ABI requires a static writable descriptor because CPython owns its internal reference-count base. Its method table is allocated once from CPython's heap under the GIL; neither object contains NeverC compilation payload.
